examples: Keep a session's changed files one click away while it works, and open a diff over the terminal.
Read and edit the session's notes or its project's huddle list without leaving the session.
Drag a dashboard widget onto the rail so it slides out over any session.
Keep every project's huddle open in the side rail while you move between sessions.
Glance at the closed rail and see how many huddle items need you without opening it.
Keep the agent's task list for the selected session in the rail, or every session's tasks in one place.
See what is scheduled for the selected session, or every global automation, and switch one on or off from the rail.
Keep tasks in the rail and flip between this session's list and every session's list with a right-click, without a second widget.
Run a quick command in the same folder as an agent, in a shell of your own, without leaving the session.
Keep one agent's notes open beside another agent's terminal while you work.
how_to: Open a session on a desktop-width window: the rail is the narrow column at the right edge of the grid.

Press a widget's icon to slide it out over the terminal; press it again or escape to slide it back (escape from anywhere but a terminal hides an unpinned bar with its panel, the last one opened first; a pinned bar stays) (a slide-out has no title bar: its lit key is the switcher).
The side and bottom slide-outs open independently, so both can be out at once; the side rail always spans the full height and the bottom rail sits between the left sidebar and the side rail.
Drag the slide-out's inner edge to make it wider (taller for the bottom rail, down to the height of the bottom strip itself), or focus it and use the arrow keys.
Enter edit layout to drag widgets onto either rail from the widget drawer, along it to reorder, onto the other rail to move across, or off both to take them out.

In edit layout, drag a widget over the slide-out's place and drop it on the top or bottom band (left or right for the bottom rail) to split the rail in two; drag the last widget out of a section to join them again.
With a split rail, a key opens its widget beside the other section's last-used one; drag or arrow-key the divider between them to resize the two, and press either open key to close.
To see every huddle list in a rail instead of the selected session's project, drop the all huddles widget from the widget drawer onto either rail; it stays put when you switch sessions.
A widget that has a local and a global variant (all huddles) wears a small globe in the lower right corner of its icon, on the rail keys, the slide-out, the widget drawer and the frame.
To follow an agent's progress, drop the session tasks widget (this session) or the all session tasks widget (every session, with the globe mark) from the widget drawer onto either rail.

To watch the pipeline, drop the pipeline widget (global, with the globe mark) from the widget drawer onto either rail; hover an add-on icon for its lag, conversations behind, last delivery and failures.

To watch schedules, drop the session automations widget (this session) or the all automations widget (global ones tied to no session, with the globe mark) from the widget drawer onto either rail; a name opens it in the automations editor and the switch turns it on or off.

Tasks, bookmarks, automations and huddle are each one widget with two views: the selected session and all sessions. Right-click its icon on the rail, or the icon at the top left of its title row, to pick the view, in or out of edit layout; the choice is kept for that placement on every device, and the all sessions view wears the globe.

In edit layout a widget that has views shows a small diagonal chip in the bottom left corner of its icon, meaning it has a menu; in the drawer's widget area the edit strip carries the same two view buttons.

The bottom bar holds the terminal widget by default: press its key to open a plain shell in the folder of the session shown, and press it again, or Escape from outside the terminal, to close it. The shell keeps running while the panel is closed.

Click a slide-out's inner edge to pin it: it keeps the agent it was pinned on, while you open other agents, a layout or Home; the pinned section's stretch of the edge turns the accent color and its bar key shows that agent's letter, unique among the pinned agents. Click the edge again to unpin.

A widget bar hides behind a thin handle: hover or click the handle to slide the bar out over the terminals, and it slides back once the pointer leaves; the pin icon at the end of the bar keeps it out. Right-click the bar (its empty space, handle or edge, or shift+f10 on the handle) and choose pin bar to keep it out; unpin bar lets it hide again.

Drag a widget bar's own border (the bottom bar's top edge, the right bar's left edge, or the thin auto-hide handle) to snap it to compact, cozy or detailed, or drag it all the way in to auto-hide; focus the border and use the arrow keys to step the size, home for cozy, end for detailed.

name: Session widget rail
summary: two widget rails hold widgets that slide out over the terminal for the active session: a side rail at the right edge (files, notes and bookmarks by default) and a bottom rail under the grid (the terminal widget and scheduled tasks by default); a new install opens both bars pinned open; the slide-out can be dragged wider or taller.
where: Open a session at 1024 wide or more: the side rail runs down the right edge of the terminal grid and the bottom rail runs under it.
Edit layout: both rails wear the dashed edit outline, an empty rail shows as a drop zone, and both take widgets from the widget drawer.
